note: The Game's own sentences (noughts and crosses): B2 at its hardest. Never used by the Board, the Ultimate Challenge or Defuse.
focus: Tenses at their hardest: perfect and continuous forms in the past, present and future.

rounds.prompt: By the time we get to the cinema, the film ___.
rounds.note: By the time + future → future perfect: finished before that moment.

rounds.prompt: I ___ here for ten years next month.
rounds.note: Next month I will reach ten years: future perfect.

rounds.prompt: His hands were black because he ___ on the car all morning.
rounds.note: A long activity up to a past moment, with visible results: past perfect continuous.

rounds.prompt: This is the third time you ___ my name wrong.
rounds.note: This is the first/second/third time + present perfect.

rounds.prompt: Don't call me at eight — I ___ dinner with my in-laws then.
rounds.note: In progress at a future moment: future continuous.

rounds.prompt: When I arrived, the meeting ___, so I missed the whole thing.
rounds.note: Finished before another past moment: past perfect.

rounds.prompt: It's the first time I ___ sushi — it's delicious!
rounds.note: It's the first time + present perfect.

rounds.prompt: How long ___ each other before you got married?
rounds.note: Duration up to a past event, with a state verb: past perfect.

rounds.prompt: This time next week we ___ on a beach in Crete.
rounds.note: In progress at a future moment: future continuous.

rounds.context: Her eyes are red and her face is wet.
rounds.note: Present evidence of a recent activity: present perfect continuous.

rounds.context: Two hours of waiting, and the bus finally came.
rounds.line: By the time the bus came, we ___ for two hours.
rounds.note: Duration up to a past moment: past perfect continuous.

rounds.context: The builders started in May and will finish in December.
rounds.line: By December, they ___ the house for seven months.
rounds.note: Duration up to a future moment: future perfect continuous.

rounds.context: Her exam is from 2 to 4 p.m. tomorrow.
rounds.line: At 3 p.m. tomorrow she ___ her exam.
rounds.note: In progress at a future moment.

rounds.context: They met in 2015 and still see each other every week.
rounds.note: Since + a past point, up to now, state verb: present perfect.

rounds.prompt: I ___ (wait) for over an hour when she finally rang.
rounds.note: Duration before a past moment: past perfect continuous.

rounds.prompt: By 2030, scientists ___ (find) a cure, I hope.
rounds.note: By + future time → future perfect.

rounds.prompt: She ___ (not/sleep) properly since the baby was born.
rounds.note: Since + past point → present perfect.

rounds.prompt: No sooner ___ (I/sit) down than the phone rang.
rounds.note: No sooner + had + subject + past participle.

rounds.prompt: I'll call you as soon as I ___ (finish) the report.
rounds.note: No will after as soon as: present perfect (or present).

rounds.prompt: I haven't seen him ___ ages.
rounds.note: For + a period of time.

rounds.prompt: It's years ___ I last went skiing.
rounds.note: It's + time + since + past simple.

rounds.prompt: By the time you read this, I ___ have left the country.
rounds.note: Future perfect: will have left.

rounds.prompt: I'd ___ been there before, so everything was new.
rounds.note: I had never been: past perfect.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Past perfect for the earlier action.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Future perfect continuous.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Present perfect continuous question.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Past perfect continuous before a past event.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: I've known her since we were children.
We've lived here for ten years.
I've seen that film last week.
rounds.answer: I've seen that film last week.
rounds.note: Last week is a finished time: I saw that film last week.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: Have you ever been to Paris?
Had you ever flown before that trip?
rounds.note: Did + bare infinitive: Did you ever go abroad? — or Have you ever been abroad?

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Rome.
I'll be knowing the results tomorrow.
Will you be using the car tonight?
rounds.answer: I'll be knowing the results tomorrow.
rounds.note: Know is a state verb: I'll know the results tomorrow.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: She's been to London three times.
She's gone to London; she's back on Monday.
She's been to the shops and she's still there.
She's been living in London since May.
rounds.answer: She's been to the shops and she's still there.
rounds.note: Been to = went and came back. If she is still there: she's gone to the shops.

rounds.prompt: Can it be continuous?
rounds.note: State verbs (know, belong, prefer) are not used in continuous tenses.

rounds.prompt: For or since?
rounds.note: For + a period; since + a starting point.

rounds.prompt: Past simple or present perfect?
rounds.note: Finished time words take the past simple.

rounds.prompt: Match each form to its meaning.
pairs: in progress at a future time
in progress up to a past time
from the past up to now
rounds.note: Four continuous and perfect forms, four times.

rounds.prompt: Match each sentence to its meaning.
pairs: She went at some time and came back.
A trip at a finished past time.
She left before another past moment.
rounds.note: Gone, been, went and had gone tell four different stories.

rounds.prompt: I started learning Portuguese two years ago.
rounds.note: Started in the past and still going: present perfect continuous.

rounds.prompt: The last time I saw her was in 2019.
rounds.note: The last time … was → haven't … since.

rounds.prompt: It's ages since we went out for dinner.
rounds.note: It's ages since + past → haven't … for ages.

rounds.prompt: This is my first visit to Japan.
rounds.note: First visit → have never been before.

rounds.prompt: The film started before we arrived at the cinema.
rounds.stem: When we arrived at the cinema, the film ___.
rounds.note: The earlier past action: past perfect.

rounds.prompt: I'll finish this book before you come back.
rounds.stem: By the time you come back, I ___ this book.
rounds.note: By the time + future → future perfect.

rounds.prompt: He went home before I got there.
rounds.note: The earlier past action: past perfect.

rounds.prompt: I haven't been to the cinema for a year.
rounds.stem: The ___ to the cinema was a year ago.
rounds.note: Haven't … for a year → the last time … was a year ago.

rounds.sentence: I've seen him at the party last night.
rounds.note: Last night is finished time: I saw him.

rounds.sentence: How long are you living in Lisbon?
rounds.note: How long, up to now → present perfect (continuous).

rounds.sentence: By the time the police arrived, the thieves escaped.
rounds.note: Earlier past action: had escaped.

rounds.sentence: She is owning two houses in the Algarve.
rounds.note: Own is a state verb: she owns.

rounds.sentence: When I will see him, I'll give him the message.
rounds.note: No will after when for the future: When I see him.

others: When I am going to see

rounds.sentence: We have been knowing each other for years.
rounds.note: Know is a state verb: we have known.
